concurrency_and_state: Single-threaded Unity UI loop drives Panel.update() and paint*(), mutating shared Panel fields (type, currentTabIndex, selected, cSelected, newSelected, currItem, vItemCombine, vMyGD, isLock, isAccept).

Async modals (ChatTextField via onChatFromMe, GameCanvas YesNoDlg/Menu via perform) retain references to mutable currItem/selected/currInfoItem; inventory/shop/trade updates or tab switches while a modal is open can leave stale or out-of-bounds state.
Panel transitions and action execution use frame counters (waitToPerform, timeShow, delayKigui) rather than event-driven state machines.
Trade lock/accept state uses client-side booleans (isLock, isFriendLock, isAccept) paired with Service.gI().giaodich(3/5/7).
cross_module_questions: Does the Java server validate Service.gI().giaodich(2, -1, -1, money) against money <= 0 when client onChatFromMe only checks num2 > Char.myCharz().xu?
Does the Java server validate Service.gI().kigui(0, ...) quantity > 0 and price > 0, and how does Panel.doNotiRuby (outside this slice) handle int.Parse errors and bounds?
If player bag/box capacity exceeds 127 slots, how do client sbyte casts (e.g. (sbyte)item.indexUI, (sbyte)GetInventorySelect_bag(...)) interact with server ReadByte/ReadSByte item slot handling?
Does the server validate skill/potential upgrade requests (upPotential) independently of the client's cMPGoc/cHPGoc UI typo and int-overflow calculations?

findings.impact: Clicking Back in the Change Flag menu unexpectedly disconnects the player from the game server.
findings.root_cause: doFireChangeFlag() creates a Back Command with idAction=10031, but perform() handles idAction==10031 by calling Session_ME.gI().close().
findings.title: Change Flag Back button (idAction 10031) closes network session

findings.impact: Non-numeric or overflowing consignment quantity input crashes with unhandled FormatException/OverflowException, and 0/negative quantities can be submitted to consignment flow.
findings.root_cause: onChatFromMe parses currItem.quantilyToBuy via raw int.Parse without try/catch and only checks > currItem.quantity without checking <= 0 or currItem != null.
findings.title: Unchecked int.Parse and missing <= 0 / null validation for consignment quantity in onChatFromMe

findings.impact: Client allows sending 0 or negative trade xu amounts if entered via text/clipboard, relying solely on server rejection.
findings.root_cause: onChatFromMe trade money branch only checks num2 > Char.myCharz().xu and never checks num2 <= 0.
findings.title: Missing <= 0 validation for trade money input in onChatFromMe

findings.impact: If bag or box slots exceed 127, item indices silently wrap to negative sbyte values, targeting wrong slots or failing server lookups.
findings.root_cause: Item slot indices (indexUI, GetInventorySelect_bag/body) are cast to sbyte before sending via Service.gI().getItem/useItem/giaodich/saleItem.
findings.title: Item slot indices truncated to sbyte in inventory/box/trade actions

findings.impact: Clicking empty slots or stale indices in new inventory, legacy bag/box, achievement, skill, or trade panels can throw NullReferenceException or IndexOutOfRangeException.
findings.root_cause: doFireArchivement, doFireInventory, doFireGiaoDich, doFireShop, doFireBox, and doFireSkill index arrays/MyVectors or dereference currItem/text without null or bounds checks (and line 10337 checks text.Equals before text == null).
findings.title: Missing null and array/vector bounds checks in doFire* handlers and onChatFromMe

findings.impact: Corrupts ItemOption template/param in-place on first compare, and causes int overflow/wrong MP cost display in potential upgrade UI when defense > 21,469.
findings.root_cause: getCompare() mutates item.itemOption[0].optionTemplate and param*=1000 in-place; doFireSkill() displays cHPGoc instead of cMPGoc for MP upgrade; cDefGoc*1000 and 500000+cDefGoc*100000 compute in 32-bit int before long assignment.
findings.title: In-place ItemOption mutation in getCompare, MP/HP typo in doFireSkill, and 32-bit int overflow in defense cost display

findings.impact: Stamina bar clipping in paintPetInfo/paintCharInfo uses wrong Y offset (X+41 / X+19 instead of 41 / 19 and missing X offset on x-coord), and the 4-arg paintCharInfo always draws stamina bar at 100%.
findings.root_cause: g.setClip passes (100, X + 41, num, 20) and (95, X + 19, num, 20) while drawImage uses (X + 100, 41) / (X + 95, 19); paintCharInfo(g,c,x,y) computes num but omits g.setClip.
findings.title: Broken stamina bar clip rectangles in paintPetInfo and paintCharInfo

findings.impact: High per-frame GC pressure and frame-time spikes when scrolling panels or closing UI/map.
findings.root_cause: paint* methods allocate strings via concatenation/Res.formatNumber/NinjaUtil.getMoneys/splitFontArray every frame, paintClans allocates new ClanImage() in paint loop, and hide()/hideNow()/doFireMap() call mSystem.gcc() synchronously.
findings.title: Per-frame allocations in paint* methods and synchronous mSystem.gcc() on panel close

findings.impact: High maintenance cost and bug divergence across parallel code paths (e.g., hide vs hideNow missing imgMap.texture cleanup and subpanel OnClose; dead loop in new inventory).
findings.root_cause: Panel God class duplicates paintEnemy/paintFriend, paintCharInfo overloads, paintItemBodyBagInfo overloads, doFireTool havePet/no-pet switches, chatTField initialization, and has dead code in paintInventory (flag=true, newSelected==0 loop) plus duplicate menu.startAt in doFireClanOption.
findings.title: God-class duplication, dead code paths, and divergent hide()/hideNow() teardown in Panel.cs
